# strict facts: a strict caller gets no "may be nil" warning for a call whose
# results the facts prove non-nil, even when the callees live in a //go:nostrict
# file: a call chain, and a cycle of functions that return non-nil values.
# A helper in the same position that can return nil still warns.
# go build and go vet must agree.

# The chain module: a strict main calls helpers in a nostrict file.
cd chain
go list -m -f '{{.Strict}}'
stdout true
go build .
! stderr 'may be nil'
go vet .
! stderr 'may be nil'

# The negative control: the same call form warns when the helper can return nil.
cd ../neg
go list -m -f '{{.Strict}}'
stdout true
go build .
stderr -count=2 'strict: warning: maybeNil\(\d\) .*may be nil'
go vet .
stderr -count=2 'strict: warning: maybeNil\(\d\) .*may be nil'

# A function that zeroes elements of its slice argument warns when the elements
# must not be nil, unless the argument gets the result. The fact passes through
# drop, a function of the package.
cd ../zero
go build .
stderr -count=4 'strict: warning: \w+ may leave nil elements in [st] '
stderr 'strict: warning: Delete may leave nil elements in s \(it clears elements of its parameter s\); use only its result'
stderr 'strict: warning: drop may leave nil elements in t '
go vet .
stderr -count=4 'strict: warning: \w+ may leave nil elements in [st] '

-- chain/go.mod --
module chain

go 1.28
-- chain/a.go --
package main

func main() {
	viaLib().Read(nil)
	cycA(3).Read(nil)
	solo().Read(nil)
}
-- chain/lib.go --
//go:nostrict

package main

import "io"

type impl struct{}

func (impl) Read([]byte) (int, error) { return 0, nil }

func viaLib() io.Reader { return inner() }
func inner() io.Reader  { return impl{} }

func cycA(n int) io.Reader {
	if n > 0 {
		return cycB(n)
	}
	return impl{}
}
func cycB(n int) io.Reader { return cycA(n - 1) }

func solo() io.Reader { return impl{} }
-- neg/go.mod --
module neg

go 1.28
-- neg/a.go --
package main

func main() {
	maybeNil(1).Read(nil)
	maybeNil(0).Read(nil)
}
-- neg/lib.go --
//go:nostrict

package main

import "io"

type impl struct{}

func (impl) Read([]byte) (int, error) { return 0, nil }

func maybeNil(n int) io.Reader {
	if n > 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return impl{}
}
-- zero/go.mod --
module zero

go 1.28
-- zero/a.go --
package main

import "slices"

type T struct{ n int }

type box struct{ s []*T }

func main() {
	s := []*T{{1}, {2}}
	b := box{s}
	n := []int{1, 2}
	s = slices.Delete(s, 0, 1)
	b.s = slices.Compact(b.s)
	_ = slices.Delete(n, 0, 1)
	_ = slices.Delete(s, 0, 1)
	t := slices.DeleteFunc(s, func(p *T) bool { return p.n == 0 })
	_ = drop(t)
}

func drop(s []*T) []*T { return slices.Delete(s, 0, 1) }
